messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] high error-rate for /v1/generate in us-east-1a (inference) — error-rate 32% over 2m; p50 latency 420ms, p95 1.6s. Trigger: 5xx ratio > 10%
PagerDuty Bot: Paging Jo (oncall) — escalation level P1 :rotating_light:
Jo (oncall): I’m on it. Pulling metrics and checking routing tables. tagging @Nora and @Samir
Jo (oncall): quick check: is this localized to us-east-1a or across the region?
Samir (infra): early view: host-level network errors on a subset of g5 hosts in us-east-1a + ENI attach throttles observed. Control plane shows increased ENI attach failures ~11:03 UTC.
Nora (neteng): seeing DNS query timeouts from that AZ to resolver fleet (us-east-1a -> resolver-proxy). Also route  table retries increase. Could be a zonal resolver saturation or AZ egress issue.
Aria (sre): customer traffic graph: notable spike in retries and downstream 502s starting 11:02 UTC, affects both hosted API and some dedicated pools pinned to us-east-1a.
Jo (oncall): statuspage impact? CS, we need any active customer reports.
Customer Success (CS): one enterprise customer reported elevated 502 errors and slow responses; support ticket #INC-9482. No broad customer outage reported yet. We'll draft comms if this spreads.
Samir (infra): I can attempt a temporary route shift for traffic served by the us-east-1a placement group: policy=latency-preferred -> fallback to us-east-1b/c for new sessions. Doing a controlled reroute for new sessions only.
Jo (oncall): good. How about existing KV cache population / hot contexts? We should avoid mass reconnects to preserve KV cache and latency.
Nora (neteng): agree — do new session steering only. I'll open a short-lived route map change: prefer az=b,c with weight 90/10 and maintain sticky sessions for existing connections.
Samir (infra): executing reroute in the router cluster now (cmd output):
```
# rolling config patch
rbxctl route apply --service=inference --region=us-east-1 --prefer-az="b:60,c:30,a:10" --sticky=true
patch id: cfg-2026-03-15-1108
```
Samir (infra): applying to edge nodes incrementally (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%)
Jo (oncall): monitoring error-rate and tails. If 5xxs drop -> good. If not, fallback to draining us-east-1a nodes.
IncidentBot: [UPDATE] reroute canary applied (5%), timestamp 11:09 UTC
Aria (sre): metrics after first canary (11:12 UTC): error-rate down to 18% overall for the service; p95 latency improved to 1.1s. good early signal.
Nora (neteng): DNS timeouts still high for us-east-1a resolvers (3x baseline). I'm going to add resolver-fallback for that AZ to use cross-AZ resolver proxies. Applying change now.
Samir (infra): note: some hosts report ENI attach rate-limit errors in cloud logs — possible AWS API throttling during large ephemeral attach churn. We're avoiding mass instance replacement.
Jo (oncall): excellent. Two parallel mitigations: routing away new traffic, and make resolver fallback so existing hosts can resolve external dependencies. Any customer impact on model loads?
Aria (sre): yes — a few model-load failures reported (S3 GET timeouts) correlated with AZ egress issues. For now, we should activate model-fallback policy: fallback to pre-warmed model snapshots in other AZs to avoid cold loads in the bad AZ.
Samir (infra): enabling model fallback across the cluster:
```
# enable fallback to cross-az prewarmed instances
rbxctl models set-fallback --svc inference --region us-east-1 --enable --fallback-azs b,c
```
Samir (infra): done. This will prefer local cache in b/c for new loads; not forcibly evicting a/cache.
Customer Success (CS): notifying the reporting customer that we have active mitigations in place and will follow up in 30m.
Jo (oncall): rolling error-rate at 11:18: 5xx ratio 9.2% (target <5%). We've reduced new-session traffic to a/c, but sticky sessions still hitting degraded hosts. Next step: partial drain of the most-reported-unhealthy nodes in us-east-1a (drain targets with rx drops > 5%).
Nora (neteng): I'll mark a set of affected racks as reduced-capacity in the routing layer to avoid noisy neighbors until AWS completes underlying remediation or we move instances.
Aria (sre): alert: KVCACHE miss-rate rose 40% due to routing shift; p99 latency blip 2.8s for a subset of customers. Monitoring.
Jo (oncall): acceptable short-term tradeoff to reduce 5xx. Keep an eye on customer-visible tail. If CS reports escalations, we may need to step up communication.
Samir (infra): evidence from cloud logs: increased ENI attach throttles around 11:00 -> 11:10 UTC, then sustained sporadic spikes. Submitted support case to AWS (case #123456789). Copying AWS support contact.
Jo (oncall): good. Any sign of zone-wide capacity loss (i.e., API for spot/ephemeral launches failing) or is it purely network/dns/eni?
Nora (neteng): I see some placement group allocation failures and slow instance launch times in us-east-1a. Could be a local capacity exhaustion combined with network control-plane congestion. I'll flag it as probable zonal capacity & control-plane stress.
Aria (sre): customer impact summary for now: partial > latency and increased 5xx for sessions pinned to us-east-1a; new sessions mostly routed to us-east-1b/c. One enterprise had degraded performance; CS engaged. No full region outage.
Customer Success (CS): drafting a short status note: "We're actively mitigating an inference degradation in us-east-1a; new traffic has been shifted to other AZs; we are monitoring and will update in 30 minutes."
Jo (oncall): action items: 1) Hold routing canary to 100% if metrics continue improving 2) Continue resolver-fallback 3) Avoid mass instance replacements to prevent ENI churn 4) Prepare customer-facing post in 30m if stable
Samir (infra): starting extended canary to 100% over next 12m. Will also throttle instance replacement automation to avoid hitting attach limits.
IncidentBot: [UPDATE] reroute at 100% for new sessions to prefer b/c, timestamp 11:29 UTC
Aria (sre): by 11:35 UTC: service-wide 5xx ratio 4.7%, p95 760ms, p50 120ms. KVCACHE miss rate returning to baseline.
Jo (oncall): OK. Looks stable. I'm going to prepare a handoff. Nora, Samir — please call if you see recurrence.
Nora (neteng): I'll keep resolver-fallback in place for 2 hours; if AWS doesn't confirm fix we'll extend.
Samir (infra): AWS support opened the case and indicates they see elevated control-plane latencies in us-east-1a and are investigating. No ETA yet.
Customer Success (CS): updated the customer with mitigation summary and timeline.
Jo (oncall): Handoff note -> Handoff to next oncall Aria at 13:00 UTC. Current state: degraded hosts in us-east-1a isolated, new sessions fully routed to b/c, resolver-fallback enabled, model-fallback active. Customer impact: limited to sessions pinned to a subset of us-east-1a hosts; enterprise customer notified. If error-rate >8% or >3 enterprise escalations, page immediately.
Aria (sre): taking handoff. I'll run a follow-up audit of drifted KVCACHE keys and check for slow cold loads.
IncidentBot: [RESOLVED?] status changed to monitoring — will auto-close thread if no regressions in 2h.
Jo (oncall): thanks team. Leaving some quick runbook notes in #runbooks/incidents for permanent follow-up (ENI attach backoff tuning + resolver-proxy autoscale thresholds).
Nora (neteng): adding follow-up action to investigate cross-AZ resolver fallback performance and TTL tuning.
Samir (infra): scheduling a post-incident sync with AWS support and infra leads.
Customer Success (CS): closing loop with the reporting customer; will await post-incident summary.
Aria (sre): acknowledged handoff. ping me if anything reappears. :thumbsup:
